title: Business license (BPOL), business tangible property and machinery-and-tools returns, and the sign permit for a glass studio
question: I am opening a glass studio that makes and sells work, teaches classes and may run a cafe. How do I get the Charlottesville business license, what classification and rate apply, and what property returns do I file?
office: Commissioner of the Revenue, business tax office (business license, business tangible personal property and machinery and tools); Neighborhood Development Services, Zoning (sign permits); Office of Economic Development (start-up help)
summary: Every business in Charlottesville needs a City business license from the Commissioner of the Revenue, applied for within the first thirty days of establishing the business (state law says before beginning business). The first year's tax is based on estimated gross receipts: a $35 fee below $50,000, $50 from $50,001 to $100,000, and above $100,000 a rate set by the business classification (state caps: retail 20 cents per $100; the Commissioner alone decides the classification, and a manufacturer selling at wholesale at the place of manufacture is exempt from license tax). A glass studio may hold several licensable activities (manufacturing and retail sales of work, instruction, a cafe), each listed on its own line of the application. File the Business License Application with the New Business License Checklist items (EIN, Virginia sales tax number, SCC registration of any trade name, the NDS Occupancy Permit for a commercial location, health permit for food) through the Commissioner's Secure Portal or by mail to P.O. Box 2964; a new license cannot be opened in the online portal. The business must be properly zoned before it begins operating. Each year by March 15, file an itemized list of equipment used in the business as of January 1 (business tangible personal property), and, if the studio is a manufacturer, the machinery and tools used in manufacturing on the Machinery and Tools return; both are taxed at $4.40 per $100 of assessed value on a 25%-to-10% age scale, billed in June and December. Renew the license by March 1 (10% penalty and 8% interest if late). A permanent sign needs a $100 Sign Permit from NDS through the Permit Portal.

steps.step: Confirm the studio is inside city limits and properly zoned
steps.how: Search the address in the Charlottesville GIS Viewer; if no record comes back, call the Commissioner's office, because the address may be in the Albemarle County part of 'Charlottesville'. The application states the business must be properly zoned before it begins operating and gives NDS at 434-970-3182. The checklist's zoning items include the Occupancy Permit for a commercial location (the certificate of occupancy from Building Inspections) and the Home Occupation Permit if you work from a dwelling. See glass_studio_zoning_use.
steps.quote: Before completing the application, verify if the proposed business address is located in the city limits of Charlottesville by searching for the address on the Charlottesville GIS Viewer . If a record is returned, proceed with the application. If nothing is found in the search, contact our office for further assistance. Your business may be located in the Albemarle County portion of Charlottesville.

steps.step: Work through the New Business License Checklist
steps.who: Operator, with the IRS, Virginia Tax, the State Corporation Commission and others
steps.how: The Commissioner's checklist lists: an Employer Identification Number (irs.gov); a Virginia Retail Sales Tax number (tax.virginia.gov), needed because sales of glass, class fees where taxable, and cafe sales carry state sales tax; registration of any trade name (DBA), LLC or corporation with the State Corporation Commission (and tell the Commissioner's office of any fictitious name); DPOR professional licenses if any; ABC licensing if alcohol will be sold; a Blue Ridge Health District health permit for food (434-972-6219); the Office of Economic Development for business resources (the checklist gives 434-825-0508; the OED page gives 434-970-3110); proof of workers' compensation for building-trades contractors; the Post Office; and City Market registration if you will sell at a City-sponsored market (434-970-3371). The signed checklist acknowledges receipt.
steps.quote: www.tax.virginia.gov - To apply for a Retail Sales Tax number

steps.step: Decide how the studio's activities will be listed, and ask the Commissioner about the classification
steps.who: Operator; Commissioner of the Revenue business tax office (434-970-3170, citycorbiz@charlottesville.gov)
steps.how: The application has lines a to e for each business activity with its own gross receipts, rate and fee. A glass studio may have: manufacture and sale of glass (state law exempts a manufacturer from license tax on goods sold at wholesale at the place of manufacture, but retail sales to the public are taxable, under the retail class capped at $0.20 per $100); classes and workshops (a service classification; the city does not publish which); and a cafe (food establishment, filed with the Meals Tax Registration). The city's pages give rates only for contractors ($0.0016, that is $0.16 per $100) and say to contact the business tax office for other classifications. The city says only the Commissioner's office determines classification and that businesses must supply documentation. Ask in writing for the classification and rate of each activity before you file, and keep separate receipts records per activity.
steps.fee: Below $100,000 of gross receipts per activity: $35 (up to $50,000) or $50 ($50,001 to $100,000); above $100,000: gross receipts times the classification rate
steps.quote: To determine the rate or fee applicable to your business activity, contact our business tax office at 434-970-3170 or citycorbiz@charlottesville.gov

steps.step: Complete the Business License Application with estimated gross receipts
steps.who: Operator (owner, partner, member or corporate officer signs)
steps.how: Fill in Section 1 (legal and assumed names, Charlottesville business address, start date in Charlottesville, EIN or SSN, entity type, mailing address, primary contact), Section 2 (any Virginia professional license) and Section 3 (each business activity with estimated 2026 gross receipts in column C for a business that began after January 1). For each activity with estimated receipts of $50,000 or less enter $35; from $50,001 to $100,000, $50; above $100,000 multiply the estimate by the rate in column D. Estimates are subject to examination and adjustment, and after the first full calendar year the tax is based on the prior year's actual receipts. Sign the oath. Building-trades contractors attach Form 61-A; a qualifying technology business may claim the credit under City Code §§ 14-13 and 14-24.
steps.deadline: Within the first thirty days of establishing the business (city page); state law: before beginning business
steps.fee: As computed on the form; check payable to 'City of Charlottesville'
steps.quote: A business entity that has been in operation less than one full calendar year must estimate its gross receipts for each business activity.

steps.step: File the application and supporting documents with the Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Two options: upload through the Commissioner's Secure Portal (choose Category 'Business License Application', or 'Food & Beverage (Meals) Tax Registration / Tax Return' for a cafe, with the Meals Tax Registration and a copy of the Blue Ridge Health District permit or inspection), or mail to Charlottesville Commissioner of the Revenue, PO Box 2964, Charlottesville, VA 22902. New licenses cannot be opened in the online Business Tax Portal. The office then sends credentials for the portal for payment, renewals and any monthly filings. A license certificate is mailed on receipt of the application and payment if no tax liabilities are outstanding.
steps.deadline: Within the first thirty days of establishing the business
steps.quote: Once received, our office will contact you with credentials for our online portal to facilitate payment of your business license, future renewals and any filing requirements.

steps.step: File the business tangible personal property return, and the machinery and tools return if the studio is a manufacturer
steps.how: By March 15 each year, list every item of property used in the business as of January 1 (furnaces, glory holes, kilns, annealers, benches, tools, torches, cylinders you own, display fixtures, computers, cafe equipment) with original cost and purchase date on the Fixed Asset / Leased Equipment Schedule; fully depreciated assets must still be reported. A manufacturer lists the equipment used in the manufacturing process on the Machinery and Tools return instead, as a separate class under Va. Code § 58.1-3507; the Commissioner must consider a bona fide independent appraisal if you ask in writing. Both are assessed at $4.40 per $100 of value on the city's age scale (25% of cost in year one down to 10% from year seven), billed in two installments on June 5 and December 5, with no proration for property sold or moved after January 1. If nothing is filed the office makes a statutory assessment. Whether the Commissioner treats a glass studio as a manufacturer for this purpose is for the office to decide.
steps.deadline: Return due no later than March 15 each year; tax installments due June 5 and December 5
steps.fee: Tax rate 4.4% ($4.40 per $100) of assessed value; assessment ratios 25% of cost (1 year old) to 10% (7 years and older)
steps.quote: All businesses located in the City of Charlottesville are required to file an itemized list of all property utilized in the business as of January 1st of each year. Filing is due no later than March 15th. The tax is split into two installments due on June 5th and December 5th.

steps.step: Register for the meals tax if the studio serves food or drink
steps.how: A cafe or any sale of prepared food or drink (including alcoholic drinks at events) makes the studio a food establishment for the City's 7% meals tax, filed monthly by the 20th. Register with the Meals Tax Registration form and a copy of the health permit when you file the business license. See glass_studio_food_and_events and meals_tax_filing.
steps.deadline: With the business license application; monthly returns by the 20th
steps.quote: Meals Tax is due on the 20 th of each month. Meals Tax is 7%. See Meals Tax page.

steps.step: Get a Sign Permit before putting up a permanent sign
steps.how: Apply in the City Permit Portal with the sign's size, shape, materials and location, lighting details and a site plan; the Administrator reviews it against the size, location and illumination standards in Development Code Div. 4.11. In an ADC, Historic Conservation or Entrance Corridor district apply for a Certificate of Appropriateness instead. Small temporary signs under 10 square feet need no permit; large temporary signs up to 32 square feet need a free permit. Inflatable, feather, neon and scrolling-message signs are prohibited. The fee is $100 per sign ($200 after the fact).
steps.deadline: Before installing, altering or displaying the sign
steps.fee: $100 per sign (Sign Permit or Certificate of Appropriateness for a sign); $200 after the fact; temporary sign permit free
steps.quote: Sign Permit Process: Before installing, altering, or displaying a sign, determine if a Sign Permit is required. (Section 4.11.3).

steps.step: Use the Office of Economic Development's start-up programs if they fit
steps.how: OED runs the GO Start-Up four-week training for City residents (free; the 2026 application is on its page), the GO Hire wage subsidy and retraining grants for City businesses (pre-application meeting required; up to $5,000 per business per fiscal year), and Minority Business Assistance. Contact 434-970-3110 or ecodev@charlottesville.gov.
steps.quote: All interested businesses must conduct a pre-application meeting with OED staff to discuss program guidelines. To learn more or schedule a meeting, please contact the Office of Economic Development at (434) 970-3110 or via email at ecodev@charlottesville.gov .

steps.step: Renew every year and report changes or closure
steps.how: From the 2026 cycle renewals are paperless in the Business Tax Portal (mailing ZIP, account number, SSN or EIN); the paper application can still be mailed with payment. Renewal and payment are due by March 1 (March 2 in 2026, the first business day), with a 10% penalty and 8% annual interest if late. Report changes of address, contact, SSN or EIN, and closures, at charlottesville.gov/cor/bizchange; unreported businesses are statutorily assessed each year.
steps.deadline: Business license renewal by March 1 each year; business property return by March 15
steps.fee: 10% late penalty plus 8% interest per annum
steps.quote: Beginning with the 2026 license cycle, the City of Charlottesville is transitioning over to a paperless renewal process.

escalation.trigger: You disagree with the classification, rate or a statutory assessment of the business license tax
escalation.next: Commissioner of the Revenue: administrative appeal of a local license tax assessment under Va. Code § 58.1-3703.1(A)(5) (the city posts an Administrative Appeals Process for Business License Assessment guide)
escalation.deadline: Within one year from the last day of the tax year for which the assessment is made, or within one year from the date of the appealable event
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3703.1(A)(5), as described on the city's Business License Tax page
escalation.quote: Pursuant to the provisions of Virginia Code Section 58.1-3703.1(A)(5), any taxpayer assessed with a local business license tax as the result of an appealable event may apply within one year from the last day of the tax year for which such assessment is made, or within one year from the date of such appealable event to the Commissioner of the Revenue.

escalation.trigger: The Commissioner's final determination on the license appeal is still disputed
escalation.next: Appeal to the Virginia Tax Commissioner under § 58.1-3703.1(A)(6), then the circuit court
escalation.deadline: 90 days from the Commissioner's final determination (§ 58.1-3703.1(A)(6); not re-read for this file)

escalation.trigger: A business tangible property or machinery and tools assessment is disputed
escalation.next: Commissioner of the Revenue: application for correction (Va. Code § 58.1-3980), or the local business tax appeal under § 58.1-3983.1 (machinery and tools and business tangible property are 'local business taxes' there)
escalation.deadline: Three years from the last day of the tax year or one year from the assessment, whichever is later (§ 58.1-3980; see business_tangible_personal_property_return.json)

caveats: The city publishes no rate table for the retail, personal service, repair, or manufacturing classifications; its pages give only the fee tiers below $100,000 and the contractor rate, and say to ask the business tax office. The classification of glass making and selling (manufacturer, retail merchant), of classes (service) and of a cafe is the Commissioner's decision.

City Code chapter 14 (Licenses) and chapter 30 (Taxation) were not read; Municode's terms forbid reprinting and the city's own pages do not reproduce them. The 2026 application cites City Code §§ 2-422, 2-423, 14-13 and 14-24 for the technology credit only.

The machinery and tools class applies to equipment 'used in a manufacturing' business (Va. Code § 58.1-3507(A)). Whether a studio that blows glass for retail sale is a manufacturer for M&T and for the BPOL wholesale exemption is not stated on any city page.

The business property filing date differs across city pages: the Business Personal Property Tax page says March 15; the Business Tax Portal page (read for meals_tax_filing.json) says January 31. This file uses the Business Personal Property Tax page.
The New Business License Checklist gives 434-825-0508 for Economic Development; the OED page gives 434-970-3110. Both are listed.
Virginia sales tax registration and collection on glass sales, class fees and cafe sales is a Virginia Tax process not modeled here.
The Office of Economic Development programs change each year; the GO Start-Up and GO Hire details are as posted on 2026-10-19.
